title: Yellow Sheet Cake with Chocolate Frosting
summary: A big, soft yellow sheet cake baked in one shallow tin and finished with a generous spread of chocolate frosting, cut into squares for easy sharing.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm metal baking tin (not glass), greased and base-lined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (about 60% cocoa solids), melted and cooled
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) with a shelf in the middle, giving it at least 20 minutes to reach temperature before baking. Starting hot and steady helps the wide, shallow batter rise evenly across the whole tin rather than doming in the centre.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat the butter, caster sugar and salt together for 4-5 minutes until pale and noticeably fluffy. This thorough creaming works air into the fat, which is essential for lift in a cake this size.

steps.title: Add eggs and vanilla
steps.text: Beat in the eggs and the extra egg yolk one at a time, mixing well after each addition, then stir in the vanilla. Adding them gradually keeps the mixture from splitting, which would otherwise trap less air.

steps.title: Mix in flour and buttermilk
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda together, then add to the batter in three additions, alternating with the buttermilk in two, mixing on low until just smooth. The acidity in the buttermilk reacts with the bicarbonate for extra lift and a soft, tender crumb.

steps.title: Spread into the tin
steps.text: Scrape the batter into the tin and spread it evenly, pushing it right into the corners with a spatula. An even layer bakes at a consistent rate, so the edges don't dry out before the centre is done.

steps.title: Bake until golden
steps.text: Bake for 28-34 minutes, until the top is golden, springs back when pressed, and a skewer comes out clean. At this point the proteins in the eggs and flour have set fully, giving the cake a stable crumb.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Leave the cake to cool completely in the tin on a wire rack before frosting. Frosting a warm cake melts the butter in the icing, so it slides rather than sits in place.

steps.title: Make the frosting
steps.text: Beat the butter for 2 minutes until smooth, then mix in the icing sugar and cocoa powder on low speed. Add the cooled melted chocolate, milk and salt, then beat for 2 minutes until light and fluffy. The melted chocolate deepens the flavour beyond cocoa powder alone.

steps.title: Frost and swirl
steps.text: Spread the frosting evenly over the cooled cake while it's still in the tin, then drag the back of a spoon across the top to create swirls. Cut into 15 squares to serve.

tips: Push the batter right into the corners of the tin with a spatula, or the cake can bake unevenly with thin, dry edges.
Let the cake cool completely before frosting – spreading onto a warm cake melts the butter in the icing and makes it slide.
Weigh the flour rather than estimating it, since too much makes the sponge dry and crumbly.
Use the metal tin specified rather than a glass one, since glass holds heat longer and can overbake the edges before the centre is ready.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store covered at room temperature for up to 3 days, or in the fridge for up to 5 days, bringing it back to room temperature before serving. Unfrosted sponge freezes well for up to 2 months, wrapped tightly.
